A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same γ-Flow Matching work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including material moved or renumbered between versions.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic-flow and latent CIFAR-10 experiments, contamination tests, sampling-efficiency results, and a neighbor-count ablation.

after.justification: V2 reports original synthetic and CIFAR-10 results, including FM+Jac comparisons, decoded-image metrics, and additional proxy and minibatch sensitivity experiments.

M1.justification: The weighted-CFM framework remains, but v2's experimental implementation uses rank-based, quantile-scaled and clipped weights rather than v1's exponential distance-based proxy (Appendices C.1 and D). Shared-time batching is now explicit; v1 does not establish whether its batches mixed times. V2's Algorithm 1 still displays the exponential rule, leaving an implementation-description inconsistency.

E1.justification: The principal CIFAR-10 task shifts from v1's stated clean-data training to a robust-target task using an inlier/outlier-class mixture and evaluation against held-out inlier-class images. This substantially changes the represented training population and generation target. The double-well, 20D ring, and Gaussian-contamination scenarios remain; v2 also reports a complementary clean-target rerun.

E2.justification: V2 adds one targeted comparator, FM+Jac, to the main quantitative comparison and decoded-sample gallery. V1 compares standard FM with γ-FM variants without this explicit-smoothing control. The optional γ-FM+Jac combination is mentioned but has no reported comparison results.

E3.justification: V2 introduces a matched-budget comparison with decoded-image FID, Recall and Coverage, fixed-step midpoint sampling, and validation-FID-informed selection instead of GSC alone. New experiments vary batch size from 128 to 1024 and dimension from 32 to 256. The main γ sweep drops γ=4. Newly disclosed architecture and training details do not establish changes to previously unspecified settings.

E4.justification: V2 adds diagnostics of distance concentration and weight stability across dimensions and batch sizes (Appendix C.1), trained-model minibatch ablations and clean-target checks (Appendix D.1), and density/weight/radial analysis of the ring example. The existing neighbor-count ablation and contamination stress plot remain. The original autoencoder reconstruction diagnostic is removed.

E5.justification: V2 first reports three-seed means and standard deviations in Table 4, identifies seeds 42, 1042 and 2042, and adds error-bar plots. V1 supplies point results and timing averages without corresponding training-seed uncertainty. This establishes new reporting, not an increase from a known v1 run count.

E6.justification: Table 1 is replaced: v1 reports γ=1 achieving inlier MMD 0.0126 versus FM's 0.0481, whereas v2 reports γ=1 with worse FID than FM (61.198 versus 59.063) and higher inlier MMD (0.000773 versus 0.000609). These are different settings, not cross-version performance changes. V2 also adds proxy/batch results and reports little clean-target advantage; the γ=4 result disappears.

T1.justification: The propositions, proofs, and Appendix A largely remain. V2 changes the diffusion flux from p∇p^γ to p^γ∇p and restores the density factor in the final roughness functional (v1 Eq. 20 to v2 Eq. 21). The flux revision fixes the double-well equation's γ=0 limit, but v2 Eq. 9 retains an incompatible 1/γ prefactor.

C1.justification: V1 claims variance-optimal estimation, transport minimization in γ-Stein geometry, and improved efficiency without sacrificing generation quality. V2's abstract, contributions and conclusion narrow these to a variance-suppression bound, idealized geometric/spectral mechanisms, and empirical evaluation under an explicit protocol. This materially reduces the claimed guarantees and generality.

C2.justification: V2 extends the existing continuum-analogy caveat to its double-well, geodesic and NFE interpretations, and treats GSC as a heuristic rather than an optimality certificate. It explains rank weights as an ordering device rather than calibrated density estimates, acknowledges fidelity costs, and limits practical benefits in light of the weak clean-target results.

D1.justification: V2 Appendix D supplies substantially more reproducibility information: training-mixture composition, autoencoder and flow architectures, optimizer and training duration, weighting and Jacobian parameters, solver settings, retrieval-bank size, and metric sample counts. It also adds a code-availability statement. Most are newly disclosed details; the PDFs do not establish that previously unspecified settings changed.

R1.justification: V2 adds Eguchi (2025) and explicitly identifies prior density-powered Stein-operator work in Section 3.4. The broader positioning relative to flow matching, optimal transport and escort geometry remains. Added bibliography entries for spectral-bias papers already cited in v1 complete references rather than introduce new research coverage.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, experimental narrative and conclusion are substantially rewritten. V2 separates latent-flow setup from a new evaluation subsection, reorganizes and expands the experimental appendices, and revises theoretical explanations to distinguish formal results from mechanisms. Cross-references and supporting document sections are also updated.

P2.justification: V2 redesigns Table 1, adds Tables 3–4 and Figures 3 and 7, replaces the ring visualization with density/weight/speed/radial panels, redraws the GSC curve, and replaces the sample gallery to include FM+Jac. Margins and figure placement change substantially. The double-well, contamination and NFE graphics are retained despite renumbering or revised captions.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially improves the paper's experimental scrutiny and transparency through an explicit smoothing comparator, fidelity/diversity metrics, three-seed sensitivity results, and detailed implementation reporting. Its acknowledgement of fidelity trade-offs and weak clean-target gains corrects important overstatements in v1. The weighting-rule inconsistency and newly introduced diffusion-prefactor error remain material weaknesses, but the clearer evidence and narrower claims provide a substantial net improvement.
